item.title: Joint Fed/OCC/FDIC/NCUA/Treasury NPRM proposes customer identification program requirements for permitted payment stablecoin issuers
item.category: Federal Reserve / OCC / FDIC / NCUA / Treasury (joint)
item.description:
Five federal agencies — the Federal Reserve Board, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury — jointly issued a proposed rule on June 18, 2026 that would require permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), as defined under the GENIUS Act, to maintain customer identification programs (CIP) comparable to those required of banks and credit unions. The proposal is titled 'Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Customer Identification Program.' A 60-day public comment period opens upon publication in the Federal Register (date of Federal Register publication not confirmed as of this entry). Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr issued a separate statement noting concern about scope gaps for secondary market transactions. The proposed rule is distinct from the April 2026 FinCEN GENIUS Act AML/CFT proposed rule, which addressed anti-money laundering programs broadly; this rule addresses the specific customer identification element of Bank Secrecy Act compliance.
Primary source: Federal Reserve Board — Press Release (June 18, 2026): Joint NPRM for CIP requirements on permitted payment stablecoin issuers — https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20260618a.htm
Relevant to: stablecoin issuers, permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, banking partners of stablecoin issuers, compliance and KYC teams

item.title: Illinois enacts first-in-nation digital-asset transaction tax (SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act)
item.description:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 3019, the Digital Asset Tax Act (DATA), as part of the state's $55.9 billion budget, making Illinois the first U.S. state to impose a transaction-based tax on digital-asset activity. The law imposes a 0.2% privilege tax on brokers who exchange, transfer, or store digital assets for customers in the state; it applies to brokers with a physical presence in Illinois or an economic nexus (more than $100,000 in gross receipts from Illinois customers), takes effect January 1, 2027, and is projected to generate roughly $60 million. The Crypto Council for Innovation has requested a line-item veto of the article establishing the levy, and The Digital Chamber and the Illinois Blockchain Association issued a joint letter opposing the measure; critics note no comparable state transaction tax applies to stocks, bonds, or derivatives.
Coverage (reporting filing): Crypto Briefing (reporting Illinois SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act; signing also reported by Yahoo Finance, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant, and others) — https://cryptobriefing.com/illinois-digital-asset-trading-tax/
Relevant to: crypto exchanges, brokers, custodians and wallet providers with Illinois nexus; payment processors; tax/compliance teams

item.title: Congress folds a statutory Fed CBDC ban (through 2030) into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644)
item.description:
On June 16, 2026, the leaders of the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees — Sen. Tim Scott, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Rep. French Hill, and Rep. Maxine Waters — released updated bill text for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644), a combined Senate, House, and White House package. According to the release and reporting on the text, the package folds in a statutory ban on a Federal Reserve central bank digital currency (CBDC): it amends the Federal Reserve Act to provide that the Fed 'may not issue or create' a CBDC or any substantially similar asset, directly or through an intermediary, through December 31, 2030; defines a CBDC as a dollar-denominated digital asset that is U.S. currency, a direct liability of the Federal Reserve System, and widely available to the public; and carves out a dollar-denominated, open, permissionless, and private digital currency with privacy protections comparable to physical U.S. currency. The reconciled text returns to the Senate floor for final action; a prior version passed the Senate 89-10 in March and the House passed its amended version 396-13 in May.
Primary source: U.S. Senate Banking Committee Press Release (June 16, 2026) — https://www.banking.senate.gov/newsroom/majority/scott-warren-hill-waters-release-updated-bill-text-on-senate-consideration-of-the-21st-century-road-to-housing-act
Relevant to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

item.title: Tribal coalition files amicus briefs opposing CFTC/Kalshi preemption of tribal gaming laws
item.category: Tribal Amici (coalition of federally recognized tribes)
item.description:
A coalition of federally recognized tribes and tribal regulatory bodies, calling itself the Tribal Amici, filed amicus briefs this month in two federal prediction-market cases, arguing that allowing Kalshi and the CFTC to override state gaming laws would also nullify tribal-state gaming compacts and strip tribes of authority to regulate prediction markets on Native land. The coalition filed a brief opposing Kalshi's preliminary-injunction motion in KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler, now before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and a separate filing in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York backing the state's opposition to the CFTC's preliminary-injunction motion. In both briefs the coalition contends that a ruling for Kalshi or the CFTC would be a 'sub silentio reversal of congressional policy and Supreme Court precedent' and would 'undermine existing tribal-state gaming compacts and regulatory frameworks' negotiated under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.
Coverage (reporting filing): The Defiant (reporting the Tribal Amici amicus briefs; links the CourtListener docket and the S.D.N.Y. filing; corroborated by Protos) — https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/tribal-coalition-amicus-briefs-prediction-markets-native-land
Relevant to: prediction-market / event-contract platforms, tribal gaming operators, sportsbooks, exchanges

item.title: Kentucky AG Coleman files three lawsuits against Kalshi/Coinbase/Robinhood/Webull, Polymarket, and VGW sweepstakes casinos
item.description:
Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman (Republican) filed three separate lawsuits in Franklin Circuit Court on June 17, 2026, targeting prediction market and sweepstakes operators simultaneously. Suit 1 names Kalshi Inc. with Coinbase Financial Markets, Robinhood Markets, Robinhood Derivatives, and Webull as co-defendants, alleging approximately $23 billion in contract volume during 2025 with approximately 89% tied to sporting events. Suit 2 names Polymarket (Catnip Inc.) and affiliated entities. Suit 3 names VGW Holdings Pty. Ltd. and affiliates including Chumba Casino, LuckyLand Slots, LuckyLand Casino, and Global Poker, targeting the dual-currency sweepstakes model under Kentucky gambling and consumer protection laws. All three complaints allege violations of the Kentucky Consumer Protection Act, the Loss Recovery Act, and Kentucky gambling statutes; relief sought includes injunctive relief and restitution. Kentucky HB 904 (Wagering Consumer Protection Act), which bans licensed sportsbooks from partnering with prediction market operators, takes effect July 15, 2026.
Primary source: Kentucky Attorney General — Press Release (June 17, 2026) — https://www.kentucky.gov/Pages/Activity-stream.aspx?n=AttorneyGeneral&prId=1944
Relevant to: prediction-market platforms, sweepstakes casino operators, crypto exchanges and brokerages enabling prediction market access, gaming operators with Kentucky user exposure

item.title: NYDFS proposes stablecoin regulation aligning New York's framework with the federal GENIUS Act
item.description:
On June 9, 2026, the New York State Department of Financial Services, under Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow, proposed a regulation to build on New York's existing stablecoin framework and align it with the federal GENIUS Act. The proposal carries forward DFS's prior requirements for U.S. dollar-backed stablecoins issued under its oversight — backing and redeemability, permissible reserves, and independent audits — and adds new federal provisions, including setting maximum amounts of reserves that can be held at any one custodian and requiring issuers to adopt risk-management programs covering internal controls, information security, internal audit, asset growth, earnings, insider and affiliate transactions, and service-provider arrangements. The proposed regulation is subject to a 10-day preproposal comment period beginning June 9, 2026, followed by a 60-day comment period upon publication in the State Register; the final regulation would take effect at the same time as the GENIUS Act becomes effective, with a one-year transition period for existing New York-licensed issuers. The Department's June 2022 stablecoin guidance remains in effect until then.
Primary source: NYDFS Press Release (June 9, 2026) — https://www.dfs.ny.gov/reports_and_publications/press_releases/pr20260609
Relevant to: stablecoin issuers, virtual-currency (BitLicense) licensees, custodians, payment-stablecoin platforms

item.title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court rules skill games are slot machines; 120-day enforcement stay issued
item.description:
On June 15, 2026, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court issued its majority opinion in J-97-2025 (Pace-O-Matic v. Pennsylvania), ruling that skill game machines 'are subject to both the Gaming Act and the Crimes Code,' overturning a Commonwealth Court ruling the Justices called 'deeply flawed.' Justice David Wecht wrote that the POM device is 'several times over' a slot machine and the legal definition 'describes the POM device with precision.' The Court issued a 120-day enforcement stay during which law enforcement cannot take action against owners and operators, and noted the General Assembly 'remains free at any time to take whatever legislative action it may deem appropriate.' Pace-O-Matic stated it is 'disappointed,' said the impact on 10,000+ small businesses and fraternal clubs presents an 'impossible choice,' and will pursue a legislative solution; bipartisan bills SB 1079 (Sen. Yaw) and HB 2213 (Rep. Burgos) are cited. Pennsylvania AG Dave Sunday called the ruling 'a significant victory for consumers, taxpayers, and the rule of law.' An estimated 70,000+ skill game machines operate in bars, VFWs, restaurants, and fraternal clubs statewide.
Primary source: Pennsylvania Supreme Court Opinion J-97-2025 (majority opinion) — https://www.pacourts.us/assets/opinions/Supreme/out/J-97-2025mo.pdf
Relevant to: skill game operators, gaming venues (bars, VFWs, fraternal clubs), payment processors, PA legislators

item.title: Fintech trade group sues Tennessee to block remittance tax (HB2502)
item.category: Financial Technology Association v. Tennessee — Davidson County Chancery Court
item.description:
As reported by The Center Square (and corroborated by Law360, CU Today, and Fintech Business Weekly), the Financial Technology Association filed suit in Davidson County (Tennessee) Chancery Court seeking an injunction to block HB2502, a law signed by Gov. Bill Lee in May 2026 that adds a $10 fee on monetary wire transfers to another country plus a 2% tax on transfers over $500 (effective Jan. 1, 2027; projected to raise more than $91 million in FY2026-27). The FTA argues the law is unconstitutional under the dormant Commerce Clause because it singles out international payments for special taxation, and its complaint states members will have to modify transaction-processing systems, compliance software, and customer-facing interfaces, incurring nonrecoverable compliance costs before year-end or risk penalties. FTA president and CEO Penny Lee said, 'when a state singles out international payments for special taxation, that is unconstitutional, plain and simple.'

item.title: Delaware (HB 441) and New Jersey (S-2141) advance statewide crypto-ATM bans
item.category: Delaware General Assembly (HB 441) / New Jersey Legislature (S-2141)
item.description:
As reported by The Defiant (and corroborated by Cointelegraph, CryptoNews, and Grafa), Delaware and New Jersey have each advanced legislation to ban cryptocurrency ATMs statewide, citing fraud losses. Delaware's House Bill 441 cleared the House Economic Development Committee and passed the House; it would require existing kiosks to go dark upon enactment and be physically removed within 90 days, bar cashier-assisted workarounds, and expose operators to unlawful-trade-practice charges plus victim-refund and forfeiture obligations. New Jersey's Senate Bill S-2141 cleared the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously and heads to the full chamber. Sponsors cited FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center data of 13,400 crypto-ATM-scam complaints in 2025 and more than $388 million in losses (a 58% year-over-year increase), with more than half of complaints involving victims over 60; operator CoinFlip urged regulation with transaction monitoring instead of prohibition. Tennessee, Indiana, and Minnesota already have statewide bans.
Coverage (reporting filing): The Defiant (reporting the Delaware and New Jersey crypto-ATM ban bills) — https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/delaware-new-jersey-ban-crypto-atms-fraud

item.title: Gensler files Sixth Circuit amicus arguing sports prediction markets are not 'swaps'
item.category: Gary Gensler (amicus) — U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
item.description:
As reported by The Defiant (and corroborated by DeFi Rate), on 2026-06-11 former CFTC and SEC chair Gary Gensler filed an amicus brief with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in KalshiEX LLC v. Schuler — Kalshi's appeal of an Ohio district court's denial of a preliminary injunction — arguing that sports-event prediction-market contracts fall outside the statutory definition of a 'swap' under Dodd-Frank and are therefore not within the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction. The brief contends the swap definition centers on hedging economic risk and that reading it to cover sports bets would imply every off-exchange wager since October 2012 had been illegal. The position contradicts the CFTC's own May 12, 2026 amicus asserting exclusive jurisdiction.
Coverage (reporting filing): The Defiant (reporting the Gensler Sixth Circuit amicus brief) — https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/gensler-amicus-brief-sports-prediction-markets-cftc-swap-rules

item.title: Wisconsin moves to block sports event-contract trading on Coinbase, Kalshi, and Robinhood
item.category: State of Wisconsin (Attorney General) — U.S. District Court, W.D. Wis.
item.description:
As reported by DeFi Rate (and corroborated by Gambling Insider and Bettors Insider), on 2026-06-09 the State of Wisconsin filed a motion for a preliminary injunction in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin seeking to block KalshiEX, Coinbase, and Robinhood from offering sports event-contract trading to people in the state until the court rules on the merits of its underlying lawsuit (State of Wisconsin v. Kalshi et al., filed April 2026). The brief characterizes the trading as 'open, repeated, ongoing criminal violations' of state law and a public-nuisance violation, argues the state's residents suffer irreparable harm from unregulated gambling, and contends the Commodity Exchange Act does not preempt Wisconsin's sports-wagering laws. The defendants have not yet responded.

item.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
item.category: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
item.description:
As reported by SBC Americas (first reported by the Associated Press and corroborated by Gambling Insider), on 2026-06-12 the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's North American Derivatives Exchange (NADEX), Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027, arguing the measure unlawfully targets federally regulated event-contract exchanges and is preempted by federal derivatives law. The enacted package (HB 757 and HB 904) also bars state-licensed gaming operators from doing business with platforms offering sports event-contract trading in Kentucky, a prohibition due to take effect next month. Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman, a named defendant, said his office 'will defend these statutes.'

item.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
item.description:
As reported by the Las Vegas Review-Journal (and corroborated by InterGame and Gambling Insider), on 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada. The Board asked the court to impose sanctions, including disgorgement of profits from Nevada transactions or daily penalties until compliance. A Kalshi spokesperson said the company has complied, attributed the issue to a technology glitch, and called the filing a 'PR stunt.'

item.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
item.description:
On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit in federal court against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. The action follows New Mexico's state-court suit against CFTC-registrant KalshiEX LLC alleging its prediction-market offerings are unlawful online sports betting. The release states New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.
Primary source: CFTC Press Release 9251-26 — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9251-26
Relevant to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges, CFTC registrants
